entry.title: Do we need Object Lock for PHI? HIPAA S3 retention: Object Lock compliance mode is not optional
entry.summary: ✓ Human-authored analysis; AI used for formatting and proofreading. The thread repeats on r/aws: a team stores Protected Health Information (PHI) in S3, has versioning enabled, and assumes that's sufficient for retention. Someone suggests Object Lock. The team pushes back. It's complex and they already have lifecycle policies. The answer: Object Lock in Compliance mode is not optional for HIPAA PHI buckets. HIPAA section 164.316(b)(2) mandates a 6-year retention period for documentation related to PHI. This is a regulatory requirement that auditors verify. Versioning alone doesn't satisfy this. A versioned object can still be permanently deleted by removing all versions and delete markers. Lifecycle policies can expire versions. entry.summary:
TypeScript brings static typing to JavaScript, but debugging TypeScript in Firefox DevTools requires some extra knowledge. Source maps are the key — they let Firefox show your original .ts files even though the browser runs compiled .js. This guide covers setup, debugging patterns, and TypeScript-specific tooling. When TypeScript compiles to JavaScript, it can generate a .map file: myfile.ts → myfile.js + myfile.js.map
The .map file tells Firefox DevTools: "line 42 in myfile.js corresponds to line 38 in myfile.ts."
